response: Yes, skin care frequency can affect the severity of incontinence-associated dermatitis (IAD) in critically ill patients. Regular and frequent skin care, including gentle cleansing, moisturizing, and barrier protection, can help prevent and reduce the severity of IAD. A higher frequency of skin care interventions, such as every 2-4 hours, has been shown to be effective in reducing the incidence and severity of IAD in critically ill patients. However, the optimal frequency may vary depending on individual patient needs and the severity of incontinence.
